name: starting architecture
last_analysis: All 9 trials scored exactly 0, both on dev and on training success. That covers bigger heads, layer-wise heads, attention, the mask as input, layout-agnostic dense heads, a pure MLP, and recipes giving up to about 426k steps. Since even the layout-free MLP never succeeds while sampling during training, an action-layout twist alone probably does not explain it. A likely shared failure is that learning collapses. Random placements mostly fill cells outside the target, so they earn negative reward, while DONE returns exactly 0. The policy can learn to stop early and then stop exploring before it can tell which placements are good. Every trial used lr 1e-3, default initialisation and entropy of 0.01 or less. Untested so far: stronger entropy, lower learning rate, normalised trunks, and near-uniform starting policies. With one round left, I put all three candidates on exploration and optimisation rather than layout.
